newsitem.title: USA: Jitney-Jungle to buy Delchamps for $213.6 million.
newsitem.headline: Jitney-Jungle to buy Delchamps for $213.6 million.

text.p: Jitney-Jungle Stores of America will acquire Delchamps Inc., another supermarket operator in the South, for $213.6 million in stock, the companies said Tuesday.

Under the definitive agreement, Jitney-Jungle will launch a tender offer of $30 for each of Delchamps' 7.12 million common shares outstandin. The companies did not say when the tender offer would begin.

Jitney-Jungle, a closely held company based in Jackson, Miss., operates 21 discount stores, 77 conventional stores and seven combination stores for 105 supermarkets and 53 gasoline stations throughout Mississippi and in Tennessee, Arkansas, Alabama, Louisiana and Florida.
Delchamps, based in Mobile, Ala., operates 118 supermarkets in Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama and Florida, and 1O liquor stores in Florida.

"The combination of these two excellent regional supermarket chains will create a very strong competitor capable of meeting the increasing challenges of the intensely competitive market in the Gulf South region," said Delchamps Chief Executive David Morrow.
Jitney-Jungle said it has commitment letters from Fleet Capital Corp. and a Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette affiliate to provide senior bank and subordinated debt financing to fund the deal.

Delchamps said its directors have unanimously approved the transaction and recommended approval by Delchamps stockholders. Credit Suisse First Boston Corp. is financial adviser to Delchamps in the deal.
Delchamps stock fell $2.50 to $29.75 on Nasdaq.
